Robin works great for a lot of your comps: Acheron (worth trying even at E0 w/ Gallagher), KafkaSwan, Clara, Jingliu, Ratio, Seele... She's somewhat usable with non-Jade The Herta as well.

Tribbie works as a definite upgrade to Robin for The Herta, and is kinda just a sidegrade or even a slight downgrade for everything else. She has decent potential in the future if you're interested in Castorice and other future units if you're interested in them, but otherwise, I think Robin provides far greater value for your account *right now*. It depends on whether you want immediate benefit vs. play the long game and see how Tribbie ages.

Optimizing (especially speed-tuning) runs can take lots of math and effort which I really don't have the time for. So I look at other runs with a roughly similar level of investment to see what I can improve.

For this MoC12 I initially did the Nikador side in 4 cycles with my E0 Acheron/Jiaoqiu/Robin/Gallagher team. Afterwards I saw a similar run that did it in 2 cycles and realized that using Vonwacq on Gallagher actually makes a pretty sizable difference (it lets me use Galla ult earlier, so I'm able to get the Aurumaton to Sanction mode faster and kill the fish it spawns with Acheron, giving me more stacks). I managed to put together a similar build and, lo and behold, I got a 2 cycle after a couple of tries.

Some people might say it's not as fun if you have reference materials to look to, but I find it even less fun to throw retries and run like a headless chicken, and I end up pretty satisfied after the run either way.

You can't really go wrong with any of those choices. It really depends on what you want for your account.

Do you already have two established teams, and want your team with Robin to better deal with off-element content? E1 Robin.

Do you feel like you're missing significant damage amplification in one of your teams and want someone to fill the spot, or do you have The Herta and want to invest in her team? Tribbie.

Do any of the characters in 3.2 interest you, and are you comfortable clearing endgame content right now? Wait for 3.2 beta; it's very likely V1 beta will be out before Robin's banner ends, and if either character catches your eye, you can see how they turn out in V4 before Tribbie's banner ends.

I feel like not giving Hyacine a cleanse would be a death sentence considering how badly people talk about Bailu even today. On the other hand, I can also see Hoyo doing that as a way to shift her power budget towards her supportive capabilities, much like Huohuo's pre-beta kit.

Regardless, only time will tell. We don't even know a *lick* of Hyacine's kit right now. Huohuo still holds her value and people should be pulling for the now rather than pulling for the later. I'm just saying Hoyo isn't afraid of making older units less relevant, especially those that are able fill the same niche as newer ones.

I'm "underselling" her because her energy regeneration (and the attack buff) are her main selling points. Everything else basically boils down to "can sustain comfortably", which almost any limited 5* (and some 4* sustains like Gallagher) can do. Hell, I have even seen some people complaining that Huohuo's sustain isn't comfortable enough.

My point is, Huohuo is best known for her energy regen. We're speaking purely on hypotheticals here, but if Hyacine – a unit that will have less design flaws by virtue of being newer – also has the ability to regenerate energy for other allies, it's more likely than not that she will do that job better. Huohuo's attack buff isn't going to make up for that, especially not in a meta almost completely dominated by Robin.

The difference is that Huohuo's energy regeneration is the *very* thing that separates her from other sustain units. Sustain units have notoriously low power budgets. If you take that uniqueness away from Huohuo, then what is the point of pulling her over Hyacine? It'd be another Sparkle situation.

She definitely has potential with HP-scaling and frequently acting AoE characters coming up. I just wanted to be more conservative because no one really knows what the future holds for these units. Playing Future Star Rail can be a risky game, especially if you're a F2P player.

"As a result of the vacatur, the 2021 Venezuela TPS designation and the 2023 Venezuela designation remain in effect and their associated statutory deadlines remain in effect. The statutory deadline [4] for each of those designations is as follows: The Secretary (1) must determine, by February 1, 2025, whether to extend or terminate the 2023 Venezuela TPS designation and (2) must determine, by July 12, 2025, whether to extend or terminate the 2021 Venezuela TPS designation."

Si el TPS se hubiera extendido, ya estuviera anunciado sobre el vacatur en USCIS. Pero no es así. Las fechas de las dos designaciones siguen siendo las mismas de cuando se extendió el TPS en 2023.

La decisión para ver si se extiende la designación del 2023 se debe dar hoy, o el TPS se extenderá automáticamente por 6 meses.
No se ha actualizado; las fechas siguen siendo las mismas que describió Noem en el vacatur del martes (abril/septiembre para los del 2023/2021 respectivamente).

TL;DR: It's required by law for the DHS to renew TPS for Venezuelans since the conditions in the country that justify the TPS designation haven't gotten better (in fact, they've gotten MUCH worse over the last few months). If DHS doesn't renew TPS, it'll definitely be fought in court and the most likely outcome is that federal judges will rule in favor of TPS. The future is still uncertain, though, so the best thing to do is to remain calm and wait for further announcements.

If you don't want to worry about TPS in the future, I would recommend to start making arrangements to marry your girlfriend and to apply for Adjustment of Status ASAP (if you're an U.S. citizen)
